name: alignair.AirrWriter
signature: (path: str, locus: str = 'IGH', columns: str | Sequence[str] | None = None, extra_columns: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> None
doc:
Incremental AIRR rearrangement TSV writer for bounded-memory streaming. Open once, call
`write(ids, sequences, preds)` per chunk, then `close()` (or use as a context manager).
`path` may be '-' for stdout.

members.name: write
members.signature: (ids: list[str], sequences: list[str], preds: list[dict], metas: list[dict] | None = None) -> None
members.doc:
`sequences` are the ORIGINAL input reads; the emitted `sequence`/`rev_comp` follow the AIRR
orientation convention per record. `metas`, if given, is a per-row dict of extra column values
(barcode/UMI/sample/cell_id) merged into each output row without overwriting model fields.

The three lists must be the same length — a mismatch (a pipeline/model defect returning fewer or
extra predictions) raises :class:`PredictionCountMismatchError` rather than silently truncating via
``zip`` and losing reads.

members.name: close
members.doc:
Close the output. For a file target, ``commit=True`` atomically renames the temp file onto
the final path; ``commit=False`` discards it (used on an aborted context exit).

name: alignair.AlignAIRError
signature: (message: str = '', *, context: Mapping | None = None, hint: str | None = None, retryable: bool = False)
doc:
Base for classified AlignAIR failures; built-in compatibility is added by subclasses.

``str(error)`` remains the plain message for existing callers. Codes and the v1
``to_dict`` envelope are the machine interface; callers must not parse messages.
Cause chains use Python's ``raise ... from ...``. Nothing logs automatically.

members.name: context
members.doc: A copy: modifying the returned data cannot alter the captured diagnostic.

members.name: to_dict
members.doc: Versioned JSON-compatible diagnostic; excludes raw causes and tracebacks.

members.name: to_json
members.doc: The error as JSON (``to_dict``).

name: alignair.Aligner
signature: (model: AlignAIR, reference: ReferenceSet, *, device: str = 'auto', model_path: str | None = None, source_commit: str | None = None) -> None
doc:
A loaded model bound to its germline reference, ready to predict. Construct with :meth:`from_pretrained` (a
local path, a shipped catalog id, or ``id@revision``); ``alignair predict`` loads its model through it.

members.name: from_pretrained
members.signature: (model: str | os.PathLike[str], *, revision: str | None = None, device: str = 'auto', reference: ReferenceSet | None = None, registry: str | Iterable[str] | None = None, offline: bool = False, token: str | None = None) -> Aligner
members.doc:
Load a model by local path, a Hugging Face repo (``hf://org/repo`` or ``org/repo`` — pulled
via ``huggingface_hub``), or a shipped catalog id (``id`` / ``id@version``), looked up in the registries of
``registry`` (a string is one registry; default: the configured ones). ``revision`` pins a
HF branch/tag/commit (or catalog version); ``token`` authenticates a private/gated HF repo (or
``HF_TOKEN``). ``offline`` uses only local caches. ``device`` accepts ``"auto"`` (CUDA→MPS→CPU). A
``reference`` that holds alleles of a locus the model does not call is refused (ConfigurationError).

members.name: save_pretrained
members.doc:
Copy the loaded model artifact into ``directory`` (for local distribution or a later
``push_to_hub``). Requires an aligner loaded from a **pickle-free** file. Returns the path.

members.name: push_to_hub
members.signature: (repo_id: str, *, token: str | None = None, private: bool = True, filename: str = 'model.alignair', create: bool = True, revision: str | None = None) -> CommitInfo
members.doc:
Maintainer-only: upload this model's ``.alignair`` to a Hugging Face repo of its own, in one commit with the
bundle's ``model_card.md`` and ``reference_manifest.json`` when they sit beside the model file (as
``alignair export`` writes them). Requires ``huggingface_hub`` and a write token (arg or ``$HF_TOKEN``). For
the shared catalog repo, use ``alignair.registry.publish``'s ``publish_bundle`` and ``upload_version``.
Returns the commit.

members.name: from_model
members.signature: (model: AlignAIR, reference: ReferenceSet, *, device: str = 'auto') -> Aligner
members.doc:
Wrap an already-loaded ``(model, reference)`` pair (e.g. straight from training), the model placed on
``device``.

members.name: bound_to
members.doc:
An Aligner that predicts from ``reference`` (its bank, e.g. a donor genotype's subset of the reference): a
copy of the model bound to it once, so later calls, and the workers a pool starts from it, use that bank
with no per-call binding; the reference is annotated against this Aligner's own (``alignair.reference.
annotate``), as one given at load is; one that holds alleles of a locus the model does not call is refused
(ConfigurationError). This Aligner is unchanged. The copy is not a model file (``model_path`` is unset), and
its label schema names the bank's alleles.

members.name: with_genotype
members.doc:
An Aligner whose calls come from a donor's ``genotype`` (``{V|D|J: allele names}``, either case): this
Aligner bound once to the genotype's subset of its reference (``bound_to``); a gene it does not name keeps all
its alleles. This Aligner is unchanged. UnknownAlleleError for an allele the reference does not hold (give its
sequence in the reference), InputError for a gene left with no allele, ConfigurationError for a key that is
not V, D or J or an entry that is not a list of allele names.

members.name: label_schema
members.doc: The identity of ``predict_raw``'s allele columns: each gene's alleles in the bound reference's order.

members.name: loci
members.doc: The bound reference's AIRR locus codes, in order (empty if it declares none).

members.name: default_locus
members.doc: The locus written for a record that carries none: the reference's one locus, else IGH.

members.name: predict
members.signature: (sequences: Sequence[str], *, ids: Sequence[str] | None = None, batch_size: int | str | None = 'auto', threshold: float | None = None, cap: int | None = None, airr: bool = True) -> PredictionResult
members.doc:
Align nucleotide strings, returning a :class:`PredictionResult` of one record per sequence, in order: every
sequence given is predicted (``read_sequences`` and the CLI drop the reads of a file that are mostly not
bases; an empty one is refused here).

``ids`` (one string per sequence) fill each record's ``sequence_id`` and the result's ``ids``.
``batch_size="auto"`` (or None) picks a device-appropriate size. ``threshold`` and ``cap`` set the called
alleles of each gene (``v_calls``...): those scoring at least ``threshold`` relative to the best (default 0.5),
at most ``cap`` of them (default 3), never none. ``airr=False`` returns light records without the AIRR
assembly. To call from a donor's genotype, predict with :meth:`with_genotype`'s Aligner.

members.name: predict_raw
members.signature: (sequences: Sequence[str], *, batch_size: int | str | None = 'auto') -> dict
members.doc:
The model's raw head arrays; label_schema describes column identity.

This method does not run the AIRR assembly. Every output uses model semantics (allele scores relative to the
read's best allele, model-frame positions). The forward is the one ``predict`` runs (``predict.forward.
run_model``: reads batched by width bucket), so the arrays are the ones a read's row comes from.

members.name: predict_iter
members.signature: (sequences: Iterable[str], *, ids: Iterable[str] | None = None, batch_size: int | str | None = 'auto', chunk_size: int = 20000, threshold: float | None = None, cap: int | None = None, airr: bool = True) -> Iterator[dict]
members.doc:
Stream prediction over an iterable of sequences in bounded memory: yields per-read records, predicting
``chunk_size`` reads at a time (a positive integer). Same options as :meth:`predict`; ``ids`` may be an
iterable too (InputError when it runs out before the sequences, or after).

name: alignair.PredictionResult
signature: (records: list[dict], locus: str = 'IGH', ids: list[str] | None = None) -> None
doc:
A typed prediction result: the AIRR-convention records plus convenience I/O. Iterable and
``len()``-able over the per-read records; ``write_airr`` emits the TSV; ``to_dicts`` returns the raw
list. The coordinates in each record refer to that record's canonical ``sequence``.

members.name: to_dicts
members.doc: The records as a list of dicts, one per read.

members.name: write_airr
members.signature: (path: str, *, columns: str | Sequence[str] | None = None) -> str
members.doc:
Write the records as an AIRR rearrangement TSV; ``columns`` selects the fields to emit (a preset name or
the field names; default: all). Returns ``path``.

name: alignair.ReferenceSet
signature: (genes: dict[str, GeneReference], has_d: bool, loci: list[LocusInfo] | None = None, provenance: Iterable[SourceProvenance] = ())
doc:
A germline reference: a ``GeneReference`` per gene, its loci and its sources. Build one from GenAIRR
dataconfigs (``from_dataconfigs``), a FASTA file (``from_fasta``), allele sequences (``from_alleles``) or its
JSON form (``from_serializable``).

members.name: gene
members.doc: The ``GeneReference`` of gene ``g`` (V, D or J, either case).

members.name: validate
members.doc: Validate selected ordered vocabularies before model construction.

members.name: locus_names
members.doc: Ordered AIRR locus codes, in the order the union was built (empty if unknown).

members.name: default_locus
members.doc: The locus a record without its own is labelled with: the reference's one locus, else ``FALLBACK_LOCUS``.

members.name: locus_mask
members.doc:
Boolean mask over the ``gene`` head selecting exactly the alleles that belong to ``locus``.

No schema (single-chain) -> all-True (unconstrained). With a schema, a locus that *has* no
alleles for this gene (e.g. D on a light chain) -> **all-False** (an explicit no-call), NOT
all-True — otherwise a light-chain read could be handed every heavy-chain D allele.

members.name: from_dataconfigs
members.doc: The annotated union of GenAIRR dataconfigs' alleles (``alignair.genairr.reference_from_dataconfigs``).

members.name: to_serializable
members.doc:
Plain-JSON-safe dict carrying everything inference needs — ordered ``names`` (== model-head
index), ungapped ``sequences``, IMGT-``gapped`` V, and junction ``anchors`` — with NO pickle.
This is the safe reference the distributed ``.alignair`` embeds and inference rebuilds from.

members.name: from_serializable
members.doc: Rebuild from :meth:`to_serializable` (the safe, no-pickle inference load path).

members.name: from_alleles
members.signature: (genes: dict[str, dict[str, str]], anchors: dict[str, dict[str, int]] | None = None, *, locus: str | None = None) -> ReferenceSet
members.doc:
Build a reference from allele sequences, ``{gene: {allele_name: dna_seq}}`` (gene V, D or J, either case).

V and J, plus D for a chain that has one (omit D for a light chain). ``anchors`` optionally supplies
{gene: {allele_name: pos}} so alleles keep their junction anchor.

The locus schema comes from ``locus`` when given (one locus over every allele), else from the allele names:
names that show one locus give it to every allele (those whose name shows none join it); names that show
several, every allele showing one, group each gene's alleles by locus (loci in order of first appearance over
V, then J, then D; the file's order within a locus); otherwise there is no schema. The alleles otherwise
keep the file's order. A chip reads its alleles from the bound reference, so the result can be bound to a
model (``predict --reference``), novel alleles included, or trained against.

members.name: subset
members.doc:
Return a new ReferenceSet keeping only the named alleles per gene (a donor's
reduced genotype), PRESERVING anchors/junction and the IMGT-gapped forms. ``allowed`` = {V|D|J: allele
names}; a segment it does not name keeps all its alleles. The kept alleles are in this reference's order, each
once, whatever order (or set) they are named in: the chip's scores depend on its bank's row order.

members.name: membership
members.doc: Each gene's per-index locus (None for an allele no locus range holds), from the locus schema.

members.name: extend
members.doc:
This reference with ``other``'s alleles added (a donor's novel or undocumented alleles), each at the end of
its locus's block in its gene; this reference is unchanged.

An allele of ``other`` this reference holds with the same sequence is skipped; with another sequence,
``on_conflict="error"`` refuses (InputError naming them) and ``"keep"`` keeps this reference's. A new allele's
locus is ``other``'s, else its name's, else this reference's only locus; one no locus can hold is refused.
A locus this reference lacks is added after its loci. Anchors, gapped forms and info come along; the
provenance is this reference's followed by ``other``'s new sources.

members.name: from_fasta
members.doc:
Load a genotype FASTA (``>allele_name`` headers + DNA). Each allele's segment (V/D/J) is read from its name
(``_infer_segment``); an InputError names the alleles it cannot be read from, and those named twice with two
sequences.

Like :meth:`from_alleles`, the result can be bound to a model or trained against.

name: alignair.TrainingConfig
signature: (dataconfigs: tuple, steps: int = 100000, batch_size: int = 64, lr: float = 0.0003, device: str = 'auto', short_boost: int = 1, grad_clip: float | None = None, val_every: int = 0, seed: int = 0, init_seed: int | None = None, max_seq_length: int | None = None, has_d: bool | None = None, model_options: Mapping = _HAS_DEFAULT_FACTORY_CLASS(), resume_path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, schedule: CosineSchedule | None = None, init_from: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, data_workers: int = 0, flanks: FlankPolicy | None = _HAS_DEFAULT_FACTORY_CLASS(), novel_alleles: NovelAlleles | None = _HAS_DEFAULT_FACTORY_CLASS(), inverted_d: float = 0.0) -> None
doc:
Reference sources plus training and model settings, every value validated here, at construction
(ConfigurationError; TrainingConfigError for the run's numbers): ``run_training`` checks only what needs the
resolved reference.

Model options are copied on construction and checked with ``max_seq_length`` and ``has_d`` as the model
configuration they build (``AlignAIRConfig``); the allele counts come from the bound reference.
``data_workers`` > 0 generates training data in that many worker processes (one per curriculum
stream at most: 28 for the default mix, 7 components of 4 streams); the batches are those of
``data_workers=0``, so it is not part of model identity.
``init_seed`` None seeds the model's initial weights from ``seed``. An int
draws them from its own seed instead, and leaves the process generators (torch's CPU one, Python's and
NumPy's) where ``seed`` left them: replicate runs of one ``seed`` then differ in their initial weights (and an
accelerator's random draws, such as its dropout) while training on the same batches.
Workers are spawned, so a script that trains with them needs an ``if __name__ == "__main__":``
guard. On an accelerator, batches are assembled ahead from the CPU random state, so a CPU random
draw in the training step or an ``on_iteration`` callback raises TrainingError;
use ``data_workers=0`` there.
``flanks`` (``data.flanks.FlankPolicy``) puts library flanks (a 5' leader, a masked primer, a 3' constant
region) around the curriculum's reads, which GenAIRR simulates bare: by default ``FlankPolicy()``, the
chip's recipe; None trains on the bare reads.
``novel_alleles`` (``train.records.novel.NovelAlleles``) draws part of the reads from synthetic novel V alleles and
puts their rows in each batch's bank (``data.novel_bank``), so the model does not memorise the training alleles:
by default ``NovelAlleles()``, the shipped models' recipe; None trains on the dataconfigs' alleles alone, as does a
run whose reference they cannot be drawn for (a dataconfig with no eligible V, loci of several species, or a custom
reference, which names no species), which says so. The model and the saved reference stay the dataconfigs' either
way.
``inverted_d`` (0 to 1) inverts the D of that share of the curriculum's records; 0, the default, trains on forward
Ds alone.
``short_boost``, ``flanks``, ``novel_alleles`` and ``inverted_d`` are the run's settings of its record policy
(``record_policy``), the rest of which is the recipe's.

members.name: record_policy
members.doc:
The curriculum record policy the run draws its records with: the recipe's, with this configuration's
``short_boost``, ``flanks``, ``novel_alleles`` and ``inverted_d``.

members.name: from_genairr
members.signature: (*dataconfigs: str | DataConfig, preset: str | None = None, **overrides: Any) -> TrainingConfig
members.doc: A configuration training on GenAIRR ``dataconfigs``, from a named ``preset`` and ``overrides``.

members.name: with_
members.doc: A copy with ``changes``.

name: alignair.TrainingRun
signature: (model_path: str, best_model_path: str | None = None, steps: int = 0) -> None
doc: A finished run: its last model, its best model (with validation) and its number of updates.

members.name: best_aligner
members.doc: The best (or last) model, loaded as an ``Aligner``.

name: alignair.compare_airr
signature: (a: dict[str, dict], b: dict[str, dict], a_name: str = 'model_a', b_name: str = 'model_b', n_examples: int = 10) -> dict
doc:
Compare two {sequence_id: row} maps. `a` is treated as AlignAIR for set-rescue (the fraction
of allele disagreements where b's call is inside a's equivalence set).

name: alignair.iter_sequences
signature: (path: str, chunk_size: int = 20000, seq_column: str | None = None, id_column: str | None = None, rejects: list | None = None) -> Iterator[tuple[list[str], list[str], int]]
doc:
The reads of ``path`` in chunks of ``chunk_size``: ``(ids, cleaned nucleotide sequences, n_dropped)`` per chunk.

Use ``alignair.io.iter_sequence_batches`` when joining source metadata or retaining original source positions.
ID state spans all chunks and grows with distinct accepted IDs; sequence payloads are chunked.

name: alignair.read_sequences
signature: (path: str, seq_column: str | None = None, id_column: str | None = None, collect_rejects: bool = False) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], dict]
doc:
Read all the reads of ``path`` at once. For large files, read chunk by chunk with ``iter_sequences``.
Returns (ids, sequences, info) with info.n_read/n_dropped/format; when ``collect_rejects`` is set,
info["rejects"] lists each dropped record ({id, position, reason, sequence}).

name: alignair.run_training
signature: (config: TrainingConfig, *, output_dir: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, out_path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, on_iteration: Callable[[TrainingIteration], object] | None = None, record_source: RecordSource | None = None) -> TrainingRun
doc:
Build, train and checkpoint a model for ``config`` into ``output_dir`` or ``out_path``.

With ``config.data_workers`` > 0, worker processes are spawned: call this under an
``if __name__ == "__main__":`` guard. On an accelerator, the step and ``on_iteration`` must not draw from
the CPU random generators: such a draw raises TrainingError, and
``data_workers=0`` is the setting for them (see ``TrainingConfig``). ``on_iteration`` is called after each update
with its ``TrainingIteration`` (``step``, ``result``: the ``StepResult``, and the batch's ``records``).
``record_source`` (``train.records.streams.RecordSource``: ``(reference, parameters, seed) -> records``) replaces
the GenAIRR provider of the run's curriculum records. ``config`` validated its values when it was built; the run
checks its reference before the model is built.

name: alignair.write_airr
signature: (path: str, ids: list[str], sequences: list[str], preds: list[dict], locus: str = 'IGH', columns: str | Sequence[str] | None = None, metas: list[dict] | None = None, extra_columns: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> None
doc:
Write a whole AIRR table at once (atomically). For large inputs, write chunk by chunk with ``AirrWriter``.
`sequences` are the ORIGINAL input reads; the emitted `sequence`/`rev_comp` follow the AIRR
orientation convention per record. `columns` selects which fields to emit. `metas` (per-row
dicts) + `extra_columns` carry preserved input metadata (barcode/UMI/sample/cell_id) into output.

name: alignair.io.MetadataIndex
doc:
Temporary SQLite lookup with atomic batch inserts and bounded lookup parameter counts.

Close explicitly or use a context manager. Missing lookups are omitted; source IDs can repeat
in a query, but stored keys must be unique. Failed inserts preserve all earlier committed batches.

members.name: put_many
members.doc:
Store ``(source ID, metadata row)`` pairs in one transaction: a DuplicateMetadataIdError (and nothing
stored) when an ID is already stored or repeats among them.

members.name: get_many
members.doc: The stored rows of ``ids`` by ID; an ID not stored is absent.

members.name: get
members.signature: (key: str, default: dict | None = None) -> dict
members.doc: The stored row of ``key``, else ``default`` (an empty row by default).

members.name: close
members.doc: Close the index and remove its file; closing twice is harmless.

name: alignair.io.SequenceReadBatch
signature: (records: tuple[SequenceRead, ...], n_dropped: int) -> None
doc: One chunk of accepted reads, and how many of the chunk's records were dropped.

members.name: ids
members.doc: The reads' ids.

members.name: sequences
members.doc: The reads' cleaned sequences.

members.name: source_ids
members.doc: The reads' ids as the input file gave them (None when the reader assigned one).

name: alignair.io.build_metadata_index
signature: (path: str | os.PathLike[str], id_column: str | None = None, keep_columns: Sequence[str] | None = None, normalize_10x: bool = False, rename: Callable[[str], str] = metadata_column) -> tuple[MetadataIndex, list[str]]
doc:
Return (owned index, output columns); close the index after joining source IDs.

``rename`` names each output column (by default ``io.airr.metadata_column``: a column AlignAIR writes becomes
``meta_<column>``) and is resolved once per output column. Colliding target columns fail before index
creation. Reading and insertion use bounded batches; every failure closes and removes the index.

name: alignair.io.iter_sequence_batches
signature: (path: str, chunk_size: int = 20000, seq_column: str | None = None, id_column: str | None = None, rejects: list | None = None) -> Iterator[SequenceReadBatch]
doc:
Yield nucleotide read batches with source IDs/positions retained across all chunks.

One allocator reserves every accepted output ID, including generated names. Rejected reads
keep their original positions but do not reserve output IDs. Unnamed reads get seq<source_index>.
Source IDs (possibly None/empty) remain separate from unique output IDs for metadata joins.

name: alignair.io.lookup_metadata_rows
signature: (metadata: MetadataIndex | None, source_ids: Iterable[str | None]) -> list[dict] | None
doc:
The metadata row of each original source ID, in order, from ``build_metadata_index``'s index (None: no
metadata, so None).

Missing/empty source IDs receive empty rows; generated output names are never inferred as
join keys. Duplicate source IDs share their metadata row; the index is queried once per distinct key.

name: alignair.genotype.genotype_bank
signature: (reference: ReferenceSet, genotype: Mapping[str, Iterable[str]]) -> ReferenceSet
doc:
``reference``'s subset of the alleles ``genotype`` names (``{gene letter: allele names}``, any case), in the
reference's order and with its locus schema (every locus stays, its ranges over the kept alleles); a gene it
does not name keeps all its alleles. ConfigurationError for a key that is not a segment (V, D, J), gene names
included, or an entry that is not a list of names (one string, say); UnknownAlleleError when it names alleles
the reference does not hold (give their sequences in the reference); InputError when it leaves a gene with no
allele.

name: alignair.genotype.load_genotype
signature: (path: str) -> dict[str, set[str]]
doc:
Load a genotype from JSON or YAML: ``{segment: [allele names]}`` (a ``{name: sequence}`` mapping per segment
works too; the sequences are ignored), or an AIRR GenotypeSet such as ``alignair genotype`` writes. Returns
``{segment: set(names)}``, segments lower-case. ConfigurationError for a file that is not such a mapping, or one
keyed by gene names. ``genotype_bank`` checks its alleles against a
reference.

name: alignair.registry.DEFAULT_REGISTRY
signature: = 'hf://AlignAIR/AlignAIR-pretrained'

name: alignair.registry.download_from_hub
signature: (spec: str, *, revision: str | None = None, filename: str | None = None, token: str | None = None, offline: bool = False) -> Path
doc:
Download a model's ``.alignair`` from a HF repo and return the local cached path. ``offline`` uses
the local cache directly (no network; a cache miss is an OfflineError). A repo, revision or file the hub does not
have is a ModelNotFoundError; a hub that cannot be reached a retryable RegistryUnavailableError; a disk error
while the hub writes its cache stays an OSError (``_hub_failure``). Requires ``huggingface_hub``.

name: alignair.registry.find_model
signature: (model_id: str, version: str | None, registry: str | Iterable[str], *, offline: bool = False) -> tuple[str, str, dict, dict] | None
doc:
Search the registries of ``registry`` in order (a string is one registry) for ``model_id`` (``version`` or the
registry's ``latest``). Returns ``(source, version, version_entry, model_entry)`` or None. Failed sources are
tried in order; if no match is found, failures are reported rather than called 'unknown model': an OfflineError
when every source failed for being offline, a RegistryUnavailableError when one could not be reached or read
(retryable when one of those is), else a RegistryInvalidError.

name: alignair.registry.is_hf_repo_spec
signature: (spec: str) -> bool
doc:
True if ``spec`` names a HF model repo (``hf://org/repo[/file][@rev]`` or a bare ``org/repo[@rev]``) rather
than a local path or a catalog id. A bare spec with a file below the repo, or one naming a ``.alignair`` file, is
a path: only the ``hf://`` form reaches a file inside a repo.

name: alignair.registry.load_registry
signature: (source: str, *, offline: bool = False) -> dict
doc:
The ``registry.json`` catalog of ``source``, checked: RegistryUnavailableError when it cannot be fetched (an
OSError for a local one that cannot be opened), RegistryInvalidError when it is not a catalog.

name: alignair.registry.maybe_notify_updates
signature: (*, registry: str | Iterable[str] | None = None, offline: bool = False, quiet: bool = False, pinned: bool = False, stream: TextIO | None = None) -> list[tuple[str, str]]
doc:
Print (to ``stream``, default stderr) one line per installed model that has a newer ``latest`` in the first
reachable registry of ``registry`` (a string is one registry; default: the configured ones). Returns the
(id, version) notices. Suppressed and swallows all errors per the conditions above.

name: alignair.registry.parse_hf_spec
signature: (spec: str) -> tuple[str, str | None, str | None]
doc:
Parse ``hf://org/repo[/sub/file.alignair][@rev]`` (or the ``hf://``-less form) into
``(repo_id, revision, filename)``. ``repo_id`` is the first two path segments; anything after is a
file path within the repo (default ``model.alignair``); ``@rev`` pins a branch/tag/commit. An InputError when it
names no ``org/repo``.

name: alignair.registry.resolve_model
signature: (spec: str | os.PathLike[str], *, registry: str | Iterable[str] | None = None, offline: bool = False, token: str | None = None, revision: str | None = None) -> Path
doc:
Resolve a model spec to a local artifact path:

* a filesystem path -> that path;
* a Hugging Face repo (``hf://org/repo`` or ``org/repo``) -> the ``.alignair`` pulled straight from
  that repo via ``huggingface_hub`` (revision/token/offline honored — the one-repo-per-model path);
* a catalog ``id`` / ``id@version`` -> the verified cached artifact from the first registry of ``registry`` (a
  string is one registry; default: the configured ones, ``resolve_sources``) that lists it.

``revision`` supplies a catalog version when no inline ``@version`` is present; for Hub repos
it overrides the inline revision. Local paths ignore it.
A pinned + already-cached version returns immediately (no network).

``shared`` names, per gene, the alleles of another
locus's block that this locus lists too (TRAV/DV alleles, which rearrange in TRA and TRD alike): they belong to
both loci (``ReferenceSet.locus_mask``).

name: alignair.reference.ReferenceSet
signature: (genes: dict[str, GeneReference], has_d: bool, loci: list[LocusInfo] | None = None, provenance: Iterable[SourceProvenance] = ())
doc:
A germline reference: a ``GeneReference`` per gene, its loci and its sources. Build one from GenAIRR
dataconfigs (``from_dataconfigs``), a FASTA file (``from_fasta``), allele sequences (``from_alleles``) or its
JSON form (``from_serializable``).

members.name: gene
members.doc: The ``GeneReference`` of gene ``g`` (V, D or J, either case).

members.name: validate
members.doc: Validate selected ordered vocabularies before model construction.

members.name: locus_names
members.doc: Ordered AIRR locus codes, in the order the union was built (empty if unknown).

members.name: default_locus
members.doc: The locus a record without its own is labelled with: the reference's one locus, else ``FALLBACK_LOCUS``.

members.name: locus_mask
members.doc:
Boolean mask over the ``gene`` head selecting exactly the alleles that belong to ``locus``.

No schema (single-chain) -> all-True (unconstrained). With a schema, a locus that *has* no
alleles for this gene (e.g. D on a light chain) -> **all-False** (an explicit no-call), NOT
all-True — otherwise a light-chain read could be handed every heavy-chain D allele.

members.name: from_dataconfigs
members.doc: The annotated union of GenAIRR dataconfigs' alleles (``alignair.genairr.reference_from_dataconfigs``).

members.name: to_serializable
members.doc:
Plain-JSON-safe dict carrying everything inference needs — ordered ``names`` (== model-head
index), ungapped ``sequences``, IMGT-``gapped`` V, and junction ``anchors`` — with NO pickle.
This is the safe reference the distributed ``.alignair`` embeds and inference rebuilds from.

members.name: from_serializable
members.doc: Rebuild from :meth:`to_serializable` (the safe, no-pickle inference load path).

members.name: from_alleles
members.signature: (genes: dict[str, dict[str, str]], anchors: dict[str, dict[str, int]] | None = None, *, locus: str | None = None) -> ReferenceSet
members.doc:
Build a reference from allele sequences, ``{gene: {allele_name: dna_seq}}`` (gene V, D or J, either case).

V and J, plus D for a chain that has one (omit D for a light chain). ``anchors`` optionally supplies
{gene: {allele_name: pos}} so alleles keep their junction anchor.

The locus schema comes from ``locus`` when given (one locus over every allele), else from the allele names:
names that show one locus give it to every allele (those whose name shows none join it); names that show
several, every allele showing one, group each gene's alleles by locus (loci in order of first appearance over
V, then J, then D; the file's order within a locus); otherwise there is no schema. The alleles otherwise
keep the file's order. A chip reads its alleles from the bound reference, so the result can be bound to a
model (``predict --reference``), novel alleles included, or trained against.

members.name: subset
members.doc:
Return a new ReferenceSet keeping only the named alleles per gene (a donor's
reduced genotype), PRESERVING anchors/junction and the IMGT-gapped forms. ``allowed`` = {V|D|J: allele
names}; a segment it does not name keeps all its alleles. The kept alleles are in this reference's order, each
once, whatever order (or set) they are named in: the chip's scores depend on its bank's row order.

members.name: membership
members.doc: Each gene's per-index locus (None for an allele no locus range holds), from the locus schema.

members.name: extend
members.doc:
This reference with ``other``'s alleles added (a donor's novel or undocumented alleles), each at the end of
its locus's block in its gene; this reference is unchanged.

An allele of ``other`` this reference holds with the same sequence is skipped; with another sequence,
``on_conflict="error"`` refuses (InputError naming them) and ``"keep"`` keeps this reference's. A new allele's
locus is ``other``'s, else its name's, else this reference's only locus; one no locus can hold is refused.
A locus this reference lacks is added after its loci. Anchors, gapped forms and info come along; the
provenance is this reference's followed by ``other``'s new sources.

members.name: from_fasta
members.doc:
Load a genotype FASTA (``>allele_name`` headers + DNA). Each allele's segment (V/D/J) is read from its name
(``_infer_segment``); an InputError names the alleles it cannot be read from, and those named twice with two
sequences.

Like :meth:`from_alleles`, the result can be bound to a model or trained against.

signature: (total: ForwardRef('float'), parts: ForwardRef('dict[str, float]'), gradient_norm: ForwardRef('float'))
doc: One update's total loss, its terms and the gradient norm before clipping.

name: alignair.train.TrainingConfig
signature: (dataconfigs: tuple, steps: int = 100000, batch_size: int = 64, lr: float = 0.0003, device: str = 'auto', short_boost: int = 1, grad_clip: float | None = None, val_every: int = 0, seed: int = 0, init_seed: int | None = None, max_seq_length: int | None = None, has_d: bool | None = None, model_options: Mapping = _HAS_DEFAULT_FACTORY_CLASS(), resume_path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, schedule: CosineSchedule | None = None, init_from: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, data_workers: int = 0, flanks: FlankPolicy | None = _HAS_DEFAULT_FACTORY_CLASS(), novel_alleles: NovelAlleles | None = _HAS_DEFAULT_FACTORY_CLASS(), inverted_d: float = 0.0) -> None
doc:
Reference sources plus training and model settings, every value validated here, at construction
(ConfigurationError; TrainingConfigError for the run's numbers): ``run_training`` checks only what needs the
resolved reference.

Model options are copied on construction and checked with ``max_seq_length`` and ``has_d`` as the model
configuration they build (``AlignAIRConfig``); the allele counts come from the bound reference.
``data_workers`` > 0 generates training data in that many worker processes (one per curriculum
stream at most: 28 for the default mix, 7 components of 4 streams); the batches are those of
``data_workers=0``, so it is not part of model identity.
``init_seed`` None seeds the model's initial weights from ``seed``. An int
draws them from its own seed instead, and leaves the process generators (torch's CPU one, Python's and
NumPy's) where ``seed`` left them: replicate runs of one ``seed`` then differ in their initial weights (and an
accelerator's random draws, such as its dropout) while training on the same batches.
Workers are spawned, so a script that trains with them needs an ``if __name__ == "__main__":``
guard. On an accelerator, batches are assembled ahead from the CPU random state, so a CPU random
draw in the training step or an ``on_iteration`` callback raises TrainingError;
use ``data_workers=0`` there.
``flanks`` (``data.flanks.FlankPolicy``) puts library flanks (a 5' leader, a masked primer, a 3' constant
region) around the curriculum's reads, which GenAIRR simulates bare: by default ``FlankPolicy()``, the
chip's recipe; None trains on the bare reads.
``novel_alleles`` (``train.records.novel.NovelAlleles``) draws part of the reads from synthetic novel V alleles and
puts their rows in each batch's bank (``data.novel_bank``), so the model does not memorise the training alleles:
by default ``NovelAlleles()``, the shipped models' recipe; None trains on the dataconfigs' alleles alone, as does a
run whose reference they cannot be drawn for (a dataconfig with no eligible V, loci of several species, or a custom
reference, which names no species), which says so. The model and the saved reference stay the dataconfigs' either
way.
``inverted_d`` (0 to 1) inverts the D of that share of the curriculum's records; 0, the default, trains on forward
Ds alone.
``short_boost``, ``flanks``, ``novel_alleles`` and ``inverted_d`` are the run's settings of its record policy
(``record_policy``), the rest of which is the recipe's.

members.name: record_policy
members.doc:
The curriculum record policy the run draws its records with: the recipe's, with this configuration's
``short_boost``, ``flanks``, ``novel_alleles`` and ``inverted_d``.

name: alignair.train.TrainingRun
signature: (model_path: str, best_model_path: str | None = None, steps: int = 0) -> None

name: alignair.train.run_training
signature: (config: TrainingConfig, *, output_dir: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, out_path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, on_iteration: Callable[[TrainingIteration], object] | None = None, record_source: RecordSource | None = None) -> TrainingRun
doc:
Build, train and checkpoint a model for ``config`` into ``output_dir`` or ``out_path``.

With ``config.data_workers`` > 0, worker processes are spawned: call this under an
``if __name__ == "__main__":`` guard. On an accelerator, the step and ``on_iteration`` must not draw from
the CPU random generators: such a draw raises TrainingError, and
``data_workers=0`` is the setting for them (see ``TrainingConfig``). ``on_iteration`` is called after each update
with its ``TrainingIteration`` (``step``, ``result``: the ``StepResult``, and the batch's ``records``).
``record_source`` (``train.records.streams.RecordSource``: ``(reference, parameters, seed) -> records``) replaces
the GenAIRR provider of the run's curriculum records. ``config`` validated its values when it was built; the run
checks its reference before the model is built.
